THE SPLIT PLATE / RECIPE

High-Protein Japanese Yogurt Hack

One 5.3 oz vanilla Oikos Pro + six HighKey mini chocolate-chip protein cookies. Press whole, chill overnight, cake-soft cookies-and-cream breakfast. 260 cal / 27g protein.

YIELD1 serving
TOTAL TIME1 min prep + 4 hr chill (overnight best)
COOK METHODSee method
EST. / SERVING~260 cal | ~27g protein

Ingredients

Ingredients

  • 1 cup (5.3 oz / 150 g) vanilla Oikos Pro yogurt — 130 cal / 20g protein on the package used
  • 6 HighKey Chocolate Chip Protein Mini Cookies (~35 g / 1 serving) — 130 cal / 7g protein on the bag used

Allergens: dairy, tree-nuts.

You want a cold cookies-and-cream breakfast that assembles in a minute and rests in the fridge overnight. The chill is what makes the recipe — pressed-in whole cookies turn cake-soft over 4+ hours. This is a high-protein take on the internet's Japanese yogurt hack — not a claim about origin or cultural authenticity.

Method

  1. 1.OPEN THE CUP. Open one 5.3 oz vanilla Oikos Pro yogurt. Leave the yogurt in its cup — this stays a one-container breakfast.
  2. 2.PRESS COOKIES IN WHOLE. Press all six HighKey chocolate-chip mini cookies straight into the yogurt. Keep them whole — do NOT crush them first. The chill is what softens them.
  3. 3.CHILL 4 HR MINIMUM (OVERNIGHT BEST). Cover and refrigerate. Four hours is the floor. Overnight is the sweet spot — the cookies turn cake-soft, not crunchy, not dissolved.
  4. 4.FOLD ONCE + EAT COLD. Give the chilled cup one gentle fold — enough to marble the cookie pieces through, not enough to purée them. Eat straight out of the cup.

SPLIT PLATE SERVING

Adult: Serve the adult portion as described above.

Kid: Serve the kid portion as described above.

If something fails

Cookies are still crunchy: Not chilled long enough. Four hours is the floor; overnight is the sweet spot. Warm-fridge sections take longer — move the cup to the back where it's coldest.

Cookies dissolved into paste: You crushed them going in or over-stirred at the end. Press them in WHOLE and fold ONCE at the end — not stir.

Not sweet enough: Vanilla Oikos Pro leans tangy. Sub Oikos Pro Cookies & Cream or Two Good Vanilla for a sweeter base — macros shift ~10 cal, protein holds within 1-2 g.

Not enough protein: Add a second cup of yogurt (another 130 cal / 20g protein → 390 cal / 47g protein total). Or drop 2 mini cookies to hold at 240 cal / 26g protein.

Portioned into a separate bowl and it's now too watery: Yogurt separates when moved. Stay in the original cup — the sealed environment keeps texture. If you're plating for a video, plate right before eating.

Storage and reheating

Store: Assemble at night, cover, refrigerate overnight. Eat within 2 days for the intended cake-soft texture.

Reheat: Don't reheat — this is a cold breakfast. Warmed yogurt breaks and the softened cookies go pasty.

Lasts: Made bowl: 2 days fridge. Beyond that the cookies over-hydrate and lose the cake-soft ping. Oikos Pro cups: per package date. HighKey bag: sealed at room temp per package.

~260 cal | ~27g protein.

Per bowl (~260 cal / 27g protein) — one 5.3 oz vanilla Oikos Pro (130 cal / 20g protein per the physical cup) + six HighKey Chocolate Chip Protein Mini Cookies (~1 serving / 35 g, 130 cal / 7g protein per the physical bag). Brands I use

Oikos Pro
Vanilla — 5.3 oz cup (130 cal / 20g protein on the bought package)
Ultra-filtered protein yogurt with a thicker set than regular Greek. Vanilla is the neutral base flavor — leans slightly tangy, which the sweet cookies balance. Product formulas shift; the physical package in hand is the source of truth for macros.
HighKey
Chocolate Chip Protein Mini Cookies (130 cal / 7g protein per ~6-cookie serving on the bought bag)
Mini format is the whole point — six whole cookies fit inside a 5.3 oz yogurt cup without crushing. Almond-butter-based, low sugar. Formulas shift; verify the physical bag before publishing macros.
